speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and feeling full in your tummy. Can you tell me if you are vomiting, and if so, does it look like it has coffee grounds in it?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. The tenderness and distension are concerning. Has he passed any gas or stool recently, and do you notice any blood mixed with mucus in the stool?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is good to know; the lack of fever and vomiting helps narrow things down. Since the abdomen is tender and distended without infection signs, did he ever pass a "currant jelly" stool (dark red with mucus), and can you show me any pictures of his belly? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdomen

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
